correctness.rationale: Unlabelled permutations correspond one-to-one to integer partitions of n, with each cycle length multiplicity m_j between 0 and fixed r. A bounded-degree Hanf locality argument makes any fixed first-order successor-language sentence eventually depend only on finitely many short cycle counts: cycles longer than J=2d+1 have the same rooted path-neighborhood, and long-cycle vertices exceed the finite Hanf saturation threshold for large n. The independent Boltzmann family Pr_t(M_j=a)=exp(-tja)/Σ_{b=0}^r exp(-tjb) becomes exactly uniform over admissible partitions when conditioned on Σ j M_j=n. The displayed Fourier lower bound on Σ_{j≤1/t}(1−cos jθ), third-moment O(t^-4) and variance Θ(t^-3), with t_n=Θ(n^-1/2), yield a span-one uniform lattice LLT and a ratio limit after deleting finitely many coordinates. Hence fixed m_1..m_J→iid Uniform{0..r}; FO probabilities have denominator (r+1)^J, while exact first-order formulas counting specified length-j cycles realize every such cylinder event, giving spectrum Z[1/(r+1)]∩[0,1]. Independently computed exact restricted-partition DP at n=20,50,100,250, r=1,2,3 and J=1,2,3; every finite-block decomposition held, and n=250 two-coordinate deviations from uniform were ≤0.023. These finite checks do not prove locality/LLT; those rely on the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The unlabelled/labelled distinction in random permutations radically changes first-order laws. This theorem gives a complete and effective FO spectrum for every fixed multiplicity cap r, a natural model between distinct parts and arbitrary integer partitions; dyadic/triadic and general base-(r+1) probabilities are genuinely nontrivial in the pure successor language. The uniform small-cycle limit, effective locality reduction and realizability form a motivated complete logical classification, not a cosmetic parameter rename.
